region.name: Seattle Metro
region.intro: Seattle is squeezed between Puget Sound and Lake Washington, so most of its geography is about crossings. I-5 and SR 99 carry everything north–south, the Ship Canal splits north Seattle from the core, and only I-90 and SR 520 cross the lake to the Eastside, where I-405 is the spine. Street names carry a sector — NW (Ballard), N, NE (U District side), E (Capitol Hill), S (Rainier Valley), SW (West Seattle), W (Magnolia) — that tells you roughly where you are.

corridors.name: I-5
corridors.desc: The north–south backbone: Everett ↔ downtown ↔ Sea-Tac ↔ Tacoma. Reversible express lanes run between Northgate and downtown, and it crosses the Ship Canal on a double-deck bridge.

corridors.name: I-405
corridors.desc: The Eastside bypass: leaves I-5 at Southcenter (Tukwila), runs through Renton, Bellevue, Kirkland and Bothell, and rejoins I-5 in Lynnwood.

corridors.name: I-90
corridors.desc: East–west from SODO through the Mount Baker tunnel, over Lake Washington on floating bridges via Mercer Island to Bellevue and Issaquah — and on to Boston.

corridors.name: SR 520
corridors.desc: The northern lake crossing (tolled): from I-5 at Portage Bay/Montlake over the Evergreen Point Floating Bridge to Bellevue, Kirkland and Redmond.

corridors.name: SR 99 / Aurora
corridors.desc: Seattle's other north–south route: Aurora Ave N through north Seattle, the downtown SR 99 tunnel (which replaced the Alaskan Way Viaduct in 2019), then south toward the airport as International Blvd / Pacific Hwy.

corridors.name: SR 167
corridors.desc: Valley Freeway — south from I-405 in Renton through Kent toward Auburn.

corridors.name: SR 509
corridors.desc: Runs south from the 1st Ave S Bridge past Burien along the west side of Sea-Tac.

corridors.name: SR 518
corridors.desc: Short east–west link from I-5/I-405 at Southcenter to Sea-Tac Airport and SR 509.

corridors.name: SR 522 / Lake City Way
corridors.desc: Lake City Way NE northeast out of Seattle to Lake Forest Park and Bothell, then freeway toward Woodinville and Monroe.

corridors.name: West Seattle Bridge
corridors.desc: The high bridge from I-5/SODO across the Duwamish to West Seattle — the only fast way in or out of West Seattle (it was closed 2020–2022 for repairs).

corridors.name: Alaskan Way
corridors.desc: The rebuilt waterfront boulevard where the Alaskan Way Viaduct used to stand; ferries leave from Colman Dock here.

corridors.name: Denny Way
corridors.desc: The seam between downtown and South Lake Union / Seattle Center — the street that marks the old Denny Regrade.

corridors.name: Mercer St
corridors.desc: The "Mercer Mess": I-5 to Seattle Center and Lower Queen Anne through South Lake Union.

corridors.name: Madison St
corridors.desc: The only street running all the way from the waterfront to Lake Washington (Madison Park), cutting diagonally across the grid. RapidRide G runs on it.

corridors.name: Broadway
corridors.desc: Capitol Hill's main street, with a Link light rail station at Broadway & John.

corridors.name: 23rd Ave
corridors.desc: Central District north–south spine from Rainier Ave up to Montlake.

corridors.name: Westlake Ave
corridors.desc: Downtown through South Lake Union (Amazon) and along the west shore of Lake Union to the Fremont Bridge; the streetcar runs on it.

corridors.name: Montlake Blvd
corridors.desc: Links SR 520 to UW and Husky Stadium across the Montlake Bridge.

corridors.name: 15th Ave W / Elliott
corridors.desc: Elliott Ave W → 15th Ave W → 15th Ave NW: downtown through Interbay and over the Ballard Bridge into Ballard.

corridors.name: NW Market St
corridors.desc: Ballard's main street, from the Locks east to 15th Ave NW.

corridors.name: 45th St
corridors.desc: Crosstown from Ballard/Wallingford over I-5 into the U District.

corridors.name: Northgate Way
corridors.desc: The main crosstown at Northgate, meeting I-5 by the mall and light rail station.

corridors.name: Sand Point Way
corridors.desc: Northeast Seattle along Lake Washington: U Village, Seattle Children's, Magnuson Park.

corridors.name: Rainier Ave S
corridors.desc: The diagonal spine of the Rainier Valley, from the Central District past Columbia City down to Renton.

corridors.name: MLK Jr Way S
corridors.desc: Rainier Valley north–south arterial; Link light rail runs down its middle at street level.

corridors.name: Airport Way S
corridors.desc: Along Boeing Field through Georgetown — the classic I-5 alternate south of downtown.

corridors.name: 1st Ave S
corridors.desc: SODO's industrial spine past the stadiums, crossing the Duwamish on the 1st Ave S Bridge toward Burien.

corridors.name: California Ave SW
corridors.desc: West Seattle's main street through Admiral and the Alaska Junction.

corridors.name: Delridge Way SW
corridors.desc: Eastern West Seattle valley route from the West Seattle Bridge south toward White Center.

corridors.name: Fauntleroy Way SW
corridors.desc: From the West Seattle Bridge through the Junction to the Fauntleroy ferry dock (Vashon / Southworth).

corridors.name: Bellevue Way
corridors.desc: Downtown Bellevue's main street past Bellevue Square, south to I-90.

corridors.name: NE 8th St (Bellevue)
corridors.desc: Bellevue's main east–west street, from downtown across I-405 toward Crossroads.

corridors.name: 148th Ave NE
corridors.desc: East Bellevue's north–south spine up to Redmond's Overlake (Microsoft).

corridors.name: Bel-Red Rd
corridors.desc: Diagonal link between Bellevue and Redmond, now a growing light-rail corridor.

corridors.name: Redmond Way
corridors.desc: Downtown Redmond's main drag, connecting SR 520 to the town center.

corridors.name: NE 85th St (Kirkland)
corridors.desc: Kirkland's main east–west road, from downtown Kirkland to I-405 and on toward Redmond.

districts.name: Pioneer Square
districts.why: Seattle's original downtown, next to the stadiums and ferry terminal.

districts.name: Chinatown-International District
districts.why: Chinatown, Japantown and Little Saigon, by King Street Station and the stadiums.

districts.name: Belltown
districts.why: Dense residential/nightlife district between downtown and Seattle Center.

districts.name: Downtown Seattle
districts.why: Retail core (Westlake, Pike Place) and office towers; I-5 walls off its east edge.

districts.name: Seattle Center / Uptown
districts.why: Space Needle, Climate Pledge Arena and Lower Queen Anne.

districts.name: South Lake Union
districts.why: Amazon's campus and biotech labs at the south end of Lake Union.

districts.name: First Hill
districts.why: "Pill Hill" — Harborview, Swedish and Virginia Mason hospitals, just east of I-5.

districts.name: Capitol Hill
districts.why: Dense, lively hill east of downtown along Broadway and Pike/Pine.

districts.name: Central District
districts.why: Historic heart of Black Seattle, centered on 23rd Ave between Madison and I-90.

districts.name: Queen Anne
districts.why: The steep hill north of Seattle Center, with the classic Kerry Park skyline view.

districts.name: Interbay
districts.why: Rail yards and industry in the valley between Queen Anne and Magnolia, followed by 15th Ave W.

districts.name: Magnolia
districts.why: Quiet peninsula west of Interbay, home to Discovery Park.

districts.name: Fremont
districts.why: "Center of the Universe" on the Ship Canal — the Troll, the Fremont Bridge.

districts.name: Wallingford
districts.why: Residential neighborhood between Fremont and I-5, above Gas Works Park.

districts.name: U District
districts.why: University of Washington and The Ave, just east of I-5 north of the Ship Canal.

districts.name: Montlake
districts.why: Where SR 520 lands — between Capitol Hill and UW across the Montlake Cut.

districts.name: Madison Park
districts.why: Lakeside village at the east end of Madison St.

districts.name: Ballard
districts.why: Scandinavian fishing-village roots, the Locks, and NW Market St.

districts.name: Green Lake
districts.why: Neighborhood around the lake of the same name, between Aurora and I-5.

districts.name: Greenwood / Phinney
districts.why: Ridge-top neighborhoods along Greenwood Ave N, near Woodland Park Zoo.

districts.name: Ravenna / Roosevelt
districts.why: North of the U District, around the Roosevelt light rail station.

districts.name: Northgate
districts.why: Mall-turned-hub at I-5 with a major light rail station.

districts.name: Lake City
districts.why: Northeast Seattle business district along Lake City Way (SR 522).

districts.name: SODO
districts.why: "South of Downtown": stadiums, port warehouses and the busway, between 1st Ave S and I-5.

districts.name: Georgetown
districts.why: Industrial-artsy pocket beside Boeing Field, on Airport Way S.

districts.name: South Park
districts.why: Small Duwamish River neighborhood across from Georgetown, by the 16th Ave S bridge.

districts.name: Beacon Hill
districts.why: Long ridge between I-5 and the Rainier Valley, with the PacMed tower at its north end.

districts.name: Columbia City
districts.why: Historic main street of the Rainier Valley, on Rainier Ave S.

districts.name: Rainier Beach
districts.why: Seattle's southeast corner on Lake Washington, at the south end of the Rainier Valley.

districts.name: Admiral / Alki
districts.why: North tip of West Seattle — Alki Beach, where the city was founded in 1851.

districts.name: West Seattle Junction
districts.why: California & Alaska — the commercial heart of West Seattle.

districts.name: Delridge
districts.why: Valley on the east side of West Seattle along Delridge Way SW.

districts.name: Downtown Bellevue
districts.why: The Eastside's skyline: Bellevue Square, Lincoln Square and big-tech offices, at I-405 & NE 8th.

districts.name: Overlake / Microsoft
districts.why: Microsoft's main campus in Redmond, along SR 520 and 148th/156th Ave NE.

districts.name: Crossroads
districts.why: East Bellevue shopping hub at NE 8th & 156th Ave NE.

districts.name: Totem Lake
districts.why: Kirkland's north-end hub at I-405, with EvergreenHealth hospital.

districts.name: Seattle
districts.why: King County seat and the largest city in Washington.

districts.name: Bellevue
districts.why: The Eastside's biggest city, across Lake Washington via I-90 or SR 520.

districts.name: Redmond
districts.why: Home of Microsoft; at the east end of SR 520.

districts.name: Kirkland
districts.why: Lakefront city north of Bellevue along I-405.

districts.name: Renton
districts.why: Boeing 737 plant at the south end of Lake Washington, where I-405 meets SR 167.

districts.name: Tukwila
districts.why: Southcenter mall and the I-5 / I-405 / SR 518 interchange.

districts.name: SeaTac
districts.why: The city around Sea-Tac Airport, along International Blvd (SR 99).

districts.name: Burien
districts.why: South of Seattle on the Sound, west of the airport along SR 509.

districts.name: Shoreline
districts.why: Seattle's northern neighbor, along I-5 and Aurora (SR 99).

districts.name: Lake Forest Park
districts.why: Wooded town at the north end of Lake Washington on SR 522.

districts.name: Bothell
districts.why: Where I-405 meets SR 522; home to UW Bothell.

districts.name: Woodinville
districts.why: Wine country northeast of Kirkland, on SR 522.

districts.name: Mercer Island
districts.why: Island city in Lake Washington that I-90 crosses on its way to Bellevue.

districts.name: Newcastle
districts.why: Hillside city between Bellevue and Renton, east of I-405.

districts.name: Issaquah
districts.why: Foothills city on I-90 at the edge of the Cascades.

districts.name: Sammamish
districts.why: Plateau suburb east of Lake Sammamish.

districts.name: Medina
districts.why: Waterfront enclave where SR 520 reaches the Eastside.

districts.name: Kent
districts.why: Warehouse-heavy valley city along SR 167.

districts.name: Des Moines
districts.why: Puget Sound city south of the airport.

districts.name: Normandy Park
districts.why: Small Sound-side city between Burien and Des Moines.

districts.name: Mountlake Terrace
districts.why: Snohomish County suburb on I-5, just north of Shoreline.

districts.name: Edmonds
districts.why: Waterfront town with the ferry to Kingston.
